args.text: [lane-marten] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to a server that has moved or been retired, so pages fail or load wrongly. (2) Slow recovery: if a site switches to a backup server during an outage, cached answers keep people pointed at the broken one. (3) Lingering bad data: a poisoned or hijacked answer stays in the cache longer, so harm lasts longer and fixes take longer to reach everyone.

args.text: [lane-marten] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail unpredictably, so a client often cannot tell whether a request succeeded, and retrying is the only safe way to recover. If the operation is idempotent (repeating it gives the same result as doing it once), a retry cannot cause duplicate payments, repeated orders or other unwanted side effects.

args.text: [lane-marten] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 (a time-ordered universally unique identifier) as a primary key: (1) it is 16 bytes, larger than a 4 or 8 byte integer, so indexes and foreign keys take more space and memory; (2) it embeds a creation timestamp, so ids leak roughly when a row was made and the order of creation, and ids made in the same millisecond may not sort strictly by creation unless the generator handles that.
